status.label: Design ready — needs approval
status.detail: Enumerated batch renames collide with still-existing source names, so the shell auto-suffixes "(2)" instead of shifting the chain.

actions.label: Design fix
actions.note: Dashboard-only action. No upstream comment or PR is posted by this artifact update.

design.root_cause: PowerRename computes the desired enumerated names correctly, but the rename worker queues exactly one IFileOperation::RenameItem per selected item in current order. There is no dependency graph or staging pass for same-directory rename chains. When bill-01-23.pdf is renamed to bill-02-23.pdf while the original bill-02-23.pdf still exists and has not yet been moved, the shell resolves the collision by creating bill-02-23 (2).pdf instead of waiting for the later rename. That makes enumeration-based shifts unstable whenever final names overlap current names.
evidence: Issue #30764 shows a pure rename-chain repro where every final target except the last is occupied by another selected source file.

CPowerRenameManager::s_renameWorkerThread groups items only by depth and then calls spFileOp->RenameItem(spShellItem, newName, nullptr) once per item; there is no same-directory collision planning or two-phase rename.
Renaming.cpp already calculates the desired final names before execution, so the incorrect (2) suffix is not a regex/enumerator generation bug.
Helpers.cpp contains GetEnumeratedFileName / unique-name utilities, which shows the codebase already distinguishes name-planning from rename execution/collision handling.

affected_files.purpose: Queues and executes the shell rename operations.
Provides unique-name helpers reusable for temporary staging names.
Allows staged-path bookkeeping when the UI stays open after rename.
End-to-end rename regression coverage for chained and cyclic rename collisions.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: The worker adds pending renames in depth-first order only. If a destination path is still occupied by another selected source item, the shell treats it as a collision and auto-uniquifies the first rename.
implementation_steps.change: Before queuing RenameItem calls, build a per-directory rename plan containing each item's current full path and desired full path. Detect blocking overlaps where a desired full path equals another selected item's current path or where the plan contains cycles.
implementation_steps.code_block: struct PlannedRename { UINT index; std::wstring currentPath; std::wstring finalPath; };\nauto plan = BuildRenamePlanForDepth(matrix[v]);\nauto [staged, direct] = PartitionBlockingRenames(plan);
edge_cases: Keep the existing parent/child depth ordering so child paths are still renamed before parents.
Treat case-insensitive path comparisons as equal on Windows.
Do not stage items whose final name is unchanged or whose collision is only with a non-selected external file.
tests: Add a chain-shift regression covering bill-01 -> bill-02, ..., bill-11 -> bill-12.
Add a two-item swap regression so cycles are covered as well.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: Conflicting items are renamed directly to their final names, leaving collision handling entirely to the shell.
implementation_steps.change: Add a first staging pass for blocking/cyclic items: rename them to unique temporary names in the same directory, commit that operation, then refresh item bookkeeping (or reacquire shell items from the staged paths) before a second pass renames them to the final planned names.
edge_cases: If the UI remains open, update item path/original-name bookkeeping after the staging and final passes so preview rows stay accurate.
Temporary names must stay in the same directory/volume to keep rename semantics cheap and atomic at the shell level.
Handle partial failure by surfacing the error and avoiding orphaned in-memory paths that no longer match disk.
tests: Verify staged chains land on the exact intended final names with no (2) suffixes.
Verify cyclic swaps (A<->B) complete without data loss or unexpected suffixes.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: Existing rename-manager tests verify straightforward rename success, but not overlapping rename chains or cycles.
implementation_steps.change: Add focused integration-style tests that create real files in the test helper directory, run RenameHelper with enumeration-based replacements, and assert that only the intended final file names exist afterward.
edge_cases: Assert that no unexpected  (2) files exist after rename.
Add a swap case (foo.txt <-> bar.txt) to ensure temp staging handles cycles, not just descending chains.
Keep folder-depth coverage unchanged so the fix does not regress parent/child ordering.
tests: Run the broader PowerRenameManagerTests suite for rename execution regressions.

verify: Build PowerRename library: pwsh .\\tools\\build\\build.ps1 -Platform x64 -Configuration Debug -Path .\\src\\modules\\PowerRename\\lib\\PowerRenameLib.vcxproj
Build PowerRename unit tests: pwsh .\\tools\\build\\build.ps1 -Platform x64 -Configuration Debug -Path .\\src\\modules\\PowerRename\\unittests\\PowerRenameLibUnitTests.vcxproj
Run the focused C++ tests with vstest.console.exe against PowerRenameLibUnitTests.dll and filters for VerifyEnumeratedRenameChainPreservesIntendedTargets and VerifySwapRenameUsesTemporaryStaging.
Run the broader PowerRenameManagerTests suite after the focused tests pass.

Manual E2E: in Explorer, select bill-01-23.pdf through bill-11-23.pdf, run PowerRename with search bill-(.*?)-23 and replace bill-${start=2,padding=2}-23, and confirm the final files are bill-02-23.pdf through bill-12-23.pdf with no (2) suffixes.
risks: A two-phase rename briefly creates temporary names; interruption between passes needs clean error handling and sensible user-visible failure states.
Path bookkeeping must stay correct if the UI window remains open after rename.
Case-only renames and mixed folder/file depths still need to respect existing shell rename semantics.
alternatives: Sorting the chain in descending order can fix the example repro but still fails swaps and more general cycles.
Leaving collision handling to the shell preserves the current incorrect (2) suffix behavior and defeats PowerRename's enumeration workflow.
Rejecting overlapping rename graphs would avoid suffixes but would unnecessarily block valid rename operations that can be completed safely with staging.
